lines.raw: Population health teams do the same.
lines.say: Population health teams do the same.

lines.raw: They **segment** (sort) the population into groups, then give each group the right kind of help.
lines.say: They segment (sort) the population into groups, then give each group the right kind of help.

lines.raw: This is called **segmentation**.
lines.say: This is called segmentation.

lines.raw: This lesson describes the groups; lesson 4 shows how a **risk score** decides who goes in which group and who gets help first.
lines.say: This lesson describes the groups; lesson 4 shows how a risk score decides who goes in which group and who gets help first.

scenes.section: Not everyone needs the same thing

lines.raw: Think of a hospital emergency room.
lines.say: Think of a hospital emergency room.

lines.raw: At the emergency room, a nurse quickly sorts patients: who needs a doctor right now, who can wait an hour, who can go home with advice.
lines.say: At the emergency room, a nurse quickly sorts patients: who needs a doctor right now, who can wait an hour, who can go home with advice.

lines.raw: This is called **triage**.
lines.say: This is called triage.

lines.raw: Segmentation is triage for a whole population, done with data, before anyone arrives at the emergency room.
lines.say: Segmentation is triage for a whole population, done with data, before anyone arrives at the emergency room.

lines.raw: The four common segments.
lines.say: The four common segments.

scenes.section: The four common segments

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Healthy**. Who is in it: No long-term illness, little use of care. Example: Lily (6) and Daniel (37). What they need: Stay healthy: yearly check-ups, vaccines, screening tests.
lines.say: Healthy. Who is in it: No long-term illness, little use of care. Example: Lily (6) and Daniel (37). What they need: Stay healthy: yearly check-ups, vaccines, screening tests.

lines.raw: **At risk** (rising risk). Who is in it: Not sick yet, but warning signs. Example: Emily: high cholesterol, on a statin since July 2025. What they need: Catch it early: lifestyle help, keep taking the medicine.
lines.say: At risk (rising risk). Who is in it: Not sick yet, but warning signs. Example: Emily: high cholesterol, on a statin since July 2025. What they need: Catch it early: lifestyle help, keep taking the medicine.

lines.raw: **Chronic**. Who is in it: One or more long-term illnesses, mostly stable. Example: Robert: type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure. What they need: Disease management: regular tests, medicine, education.
lines.say: Chronic. Who is in it: One or more long-term illnesses, mostly stable. Example: Robert: type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure. What they need: Disease management: regular tests, medicine, education.

lines.raw: **Complex** (high risk). Who is in it: Several serious illnesses, frequent hospital stays. Example: A fictional member with heart failure, diabetes and kidney disease, admitted twice this year. What they need: Care management: a nurse who coordinates everything.
lines.say: Complex (high risk). Who is in it: Several serious illnesses, frequent hospital stays. Example: A fictional member with heart failure, diabetes and kidney disease, admitted twice this year. What they need: Care management: a nurse who coordinates everything.

scenes.section: The four common segments

lines.raw: Names vary.
lines.say: Names vary.

lines.raw: Different companies use different labels and numbers of groups: "low / medium / high risk", "well / rising risk / chronic / catastrophic", or five or six tiers.
lines.say: Different companies use different labels and numbers of groups: "low or medium or high risk", "well or rising risk or chronic or catastrophic", or five or six tiers.

lines.raw: The idea is always the same: sort people by how much help they need.
lines.say: The idea is always the same: sort people by how much help they need.

lines.raw: This is the most important fact in population health.
lines.say: This is the most important fact in population health.

lines.raw: US government survey data has shown the same pattern for many years: roughly **5% of people account for about half of all healthcare spending**, while the healthiest half of people account for only a few percent.
lines.say: U S government survey data has shown the same pattern for many years: roughly 5 percent of people account for about half of all healthcare spending, while the healthiest half of people account for only a few percent.

lines.raw: An illustrative plan: 1,000 members, all covered for 12 months, $6,000,000 total cost.
lines.say: An illustrative plan: 1,000 members, all covered for 12 months, 6000000 dollars total cost.

lines.raw: Healthy. Members: 550. % of members: 55%. Cost per member per year: $1,200. Total cost: $660,000. % of cost: 11%. PMPM (per member per month): $100.
lines.say: Healthy. Members: 550. % of members: 55 percent. Cost per member per year: 1200 dollars. Total cost: 660000 dollars. % of cost: 11 percent. P M P M (per member per month): 100 dollars.

lines.raw: At risk. Members: 250. % of members: 25%. Cost per member per year: $3,600. Total cost: $900,000. % of cost: 15%. PMPM (per member per month): $300.
lines.say: At risk. Members: 250. % of members: 25 percent. Cost per member per year: 3600 dollars. Total cost: 900000 dollars. % of cost: 15 percent. P M P M (per member per month): 300 dollars.

lines.raw: Chronic. Members: 150. % of members: 15%. Cost per member per year: $9,600. Total cost: $1,440,000. % of cost: 24%. PMPM (per member per month): $800.
lines.say: Chronic. Members: 150. % of members: 15 percent. Cost per member per year: 9600 dollars. Total cost: 1440000 dollars. % of cost: 24 percent. P M P M (per member per month): 800 dollars.

lines.raw: Complex. Members: 50. % of members: 5%. Cost per member per year: $60,000. Total cost: $3,000,000. % of cost: 50%. PMPM (per member per month): $5,000.
lines.say: Complex. Members: 50. % of members: 5 percent. Cost per member per year: 60000 dollars. Total cost: 3000000 dollars. % of cost: 50 percent. P M P M (per member per month): 5000 dollars.

lines.raw: **Total**. Members: **1,000**. % of members: **100%**. Cost per member per year: **$6,000**. Total cost: **$6,000,000**. % of cost: **100%**. PMPM (per member per month): **$500**.
lines.say: Total. Members: 1,000. % of members: 100 percent. Cost per member per year: 6000 dollars. Total cost: 6000000 dollars. % of cost: 100 percent. P M P M (per member per month): 500 dollars.

scenes.section: A few people use most of the money

lines.raw: Check the maths.
lines.say: Check the maths.
Total cost: 660000 dollars and 900000 dollars and 1440000 dollars and 3000000 dollars = 6000000 dollars ✓.
Member months: 1,000 × 12 = 12,000, so P M P M = 6000000 dollars ÷ 12,000 = 500 dollars ✓.

lines.raw: Complex PMPM: $60,000 ÷ 12 = **$5,000**, which is **50 times** the healthy PMPM of $100.
lines.say: Complex P M P M: 60000 dollars ÷ 12 = 5000 dollars which is 50 times the healthy P M P M of 100 dollars.

scenes.section: A few people use most of the money

lines.raw: PMPM (per member per month), also explained in the Eligibility course.
lines.say: P M P M (per member per month), also explained in the Eligibility course.

lines.raw: PMPM equals Total cost ÷ Member months.
lines.say: P M P M equals Total cost ÷ Member months.

lines.raw: For example: Chronic segment: $1,440,000 ÷ (150 times 12) equals $1,440,000 ÷ 1,800 equals $800 PMPM.
lines.say: For example: Chronic segment: 1440000 dollars ÷ (150 times 12) equals 1440000 dollars ÷ 1,800 equals 800 dollars P M P M.

scenes.section: Registries: the list for one condition

lines.raw: Registers you may have seen in Nepal.
lines.say: Registers you may have seen in Nepal.

lines.raw: A health post keeps a **register of pregnant women** in its area, so staff can check who has missed an antenatal check-up.
lines.say: A health post keeps a register of pregnant women in its area, so staff can check who has missed an antenatal check-up.

lines.raw: TB treatment centres keep a **TB register**: every patient on treatment, when they started and whether they are taking their medicine.
lines.say: T B treatment centres keep a T B register: every patient on treatment, when they started and whether they are taking their medicine.

lines.raw: An FCHV's notebook of households is a register too.
lines.say: An FCHV's notebook of households is a register too.

lines.raw: The common idea: a **list of people with one condition**, kept up to date, with what is still due for each one, so nobody is forgotten.
lines.say: The common idea: a list of people with one condition, kept up to date, with what is still due for each one, so nobody is forgotten.

scenes.section: Registries: the list for one condition

lines.raw: In the US, this list is called a **registry**.
lines.say: In the U S, this list is called a registry.

lines.raw: The most common one is the **diabetes registry**.
lines.say: The most common one is the diabetes registry.

lines.raw: It lists every member who has diabetes, with their latest test results and which recommended care they have or have not had this year.
lines.say: It lists every member who has diabetes, with their latest test results and which recommended care they have or have not had this year.

lines.raw: The missing items are called **gaps in care**.
lines.say: The missing items are called gaps in care.

lines.say: A diabetes registry (one row per person, as of 31 December 2025).

lines.say: For teaching, this course puts members of two different insurers in one small sample: Maria from an employer plan, and Robert and Thomas from Gulf Coast Health Plan's Medicare Advantage plan.

lines.say: Higher is worse.

lines.say: Many U S quality measures (for example, the HEDIS measures, short for Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set, used to rate health plans) check exactly these things: did people with diabetes get an eye exam, is their A1c controlled?

lines.raw: Why it matters for data.

lines.raw: A segment and a registry are both **snapshots**.
lines.say: A segment and a registry are both snapshots.

lines.raw: Store them with an **as-of date** (for example `segment_asof = 2025-12-31`), and keep the history, so you can later ask "who moved from at risk to chronic this year?".
lines.say: Store them with an as-of date (for example s e g m e n t _ a s o f = 2 0 2 5 dash 1 2 dash 3 1), and keep the history, so you can later ask "who moved from at risk to chronic this year?".

lines.raw: Without dates, last month's list silently overwrites this month's, and nobody can check whether a programme moved people to a better segment.
lines.say: Without dates, last month's list silently overwrites this month's, and nobody can check whether a programme moved people to a better segment.

scenes.section: Key takeaways

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: Segmentation sorts the population into groups that need different help: healthy, at risk, chronic, complex.
lines.say: Segmentation sorts the population into groups that need different help: healthy, at risk, chronic, complex.

lines.raw: A small share of people accounts for a large share of US healthcare spending, so the complex group gets the most attention.
lines.say: A small share of people accounts for a large share of U S healthcare spending, so the complex group gets the most attention.

lines.raw: People move between segments; one expensive year (like Emily's surgery) does not always mean high risk.
lines.say: People move between segments; one expensive year (like Emily's surgery) does not always mean high risk.

lines.raw: A registry is a list of everyone with one condition, used to find gaps in care.
lines.say: A registry is a list of everyone with one condition, used to find gaps in care.
